limitations: Single request per mode/size/block: latency quantiles are not distribution estimates.
Adaptive platform counts are not exact client counts; windows combine modes and, for ascending, sizes.
Memory quantiles describe shared isolate observations, not per-request peaks or an OOM immunity guarantee.
The ordinary wrapper does not drain request background work; client cap1 is not a bound on all isolate work.
Changed order is not a controlled cold-isolate experiment; size, GC, routing and earlier history can affect measurements.
Baseline original upload did not record a launch source hash; active identities and later source inventory retain that limitation.
Launch provenance reuses active-version records; this archive does not claim a separate live deployment check at each large-run start.
These whole-stack results do not establish the isolated resource effect of JSON-origin compression.
